decisive_items: a 17 × 9 cm mixed solid and cystic mass occupying the right hepatic lobe
an infrarenal IVC thrombus and a near-occlusive embolus in the left pulmonary artery
compression of the distal IVC at its junction with the right atrium
response.rationale: The hepatic mass in a child is the primary pathology; hepatoblastoma is the most likely cause, with IVC thrombus and pulmonary embolus as secondary complications. Other candidates describe consequences or findings, not the underlying diagnosis.

rejected.why: Abdominal compartment syndrome is a clinical concern, not the underlying cause of the mass and embolic events.
Pulmonary embolism is a complication of the IVC thrombus, not the primary diagnosis.
Embolic disease is a mechanism, not a specific diagnosis; it results from the tumor-associated thrombus.
IVC thrombosis is a secondary finding, not the most likely primary diagnosis in this pediatric hepatic mass case.
